brief: UBS's daily Asia note leads with NVIDIA's Q3 beat: profit and revenue topped estimates, Q4 revenue was guided to about USD 130bn, and next fiscal year revenue growth was raised to 75% from 70%. Shares rose 4.9% after-hours despite the Nasdaq closing 0.7% lower beforehand on chip-demand and capex-sustainability worries. UBS reiterates AI as a structural opportunity, citing robust demand against tight compute supply, and raises its own aggregate AI capex forecast to USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028, with cloud growth and consumer AI agents as further demand drivers. It argues recent volatility does not derail the thesis but says the AI trade is growing more sensitive to geopolitical and macro developments, with monetization (nearly USD 3tr to be deployed over two years) the ultimate test. Two risk threads follow: new US chip export restrictions on China and other adversaries, which UBS expects to have limited revenue impact but could pressure above-UBS 2028 capex consensus and invite state-level restrictions after the midterms; and a longer Fed hiking cycle raising AI financing risk, with stress already visible among leveraged infrastructure providers. UBS recommends staying engaged but more selective, favoring financially strong tech platforms and durable semiconductor/hardware names, balanced with defensive tech and broader diversification.
